issues.location: first paragraph after the limitation-of-size principle, image-cardinality comparison
issues.finding: The source infers cardle(image(tau,A),A) merely because the image is generated from A. Earlier in the corpus, cardle means existence of an injection (content/sets-functions-relations/size-of-sets/comparing-size.tex, lines 27-28). The defining map A onto its image is surjective; in ZF without Choice, an arbitrary surjection need not provide an injection of its range back into its domain. Thus the displayed cardinal comparison does not follow from Replacement alone.
issues.proposed_resolution: Keep the displayed comparison as a named, unproved claim and explicitly say it does not follow without Choice. Use the valid surjective-image fact for the informal size argument, conditional on interpreting 'not too many' as closed under surjective images.

translation_treatment: The target says the image is a surjective image of its source and flags the displayed injection-based cardinal bound as requiring Choice. It states the limitation-of-size inference conditionally on closure under surjective images. The displayed formula is retained for precise reference but is not asserted. Frozen source bytes are unchanged.
